rows.title: Transformers as amortized Bayesian inference: approximation and generalization
rows.domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
rows.statement: Müller et al. train transformers on datasets sampled from a prior over data-generating processes so that the network outputs the posterior predictive distribution (prior-data fitted networks). Give quantitative guarantees: for a given prior (e.g. a Gaussian process prior), bound the size of transformer needed to approximate the posterior predictive within epsilon in KL uniformly over datasets of size N, and the number of pretraining datasets needed, and show that the pretrained network's predictions converge to the Bayes predictor as both grow.
rows.statement_caveat: Empirical results are strong (e.g. TabPFN); theory is limited to consistency-type arguments (to verify).
rows.source: S. Müller, N. Hollmann, S. Pineda Arango, J. Grabocka and F. Hutter, Transformers Can Do Bayesian Inference, arXiv:2112.10510 (2021)
rows.locator: to verify: Müller et al., discussion of theory.
rows.why_important: Amortized inference by sequence models is how in-context learning is used in practice; its guarantees are a question about approximating posterior maps.
rows.where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
rows.note: Fame: ICLR 2022; TabPFN (Nature 2025, to verify) made the approach widely used.

rows.title: Convergence of Adam with the hyperparameters used in practice
rows.domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
rows.statement: Reddi, Kale and Kumar construct convex problems where Adam with fixed beta_1, beta_2 diverges. Zhang et al. show Adam converges to a neighbourhood of stationary points for smooth nonconvex objectives when beta_2 is chosen large depending on the problem (after beta_1, n are fixed). Prove (or disprove) that Adam with beta_1 < sqrt(beta_2), beta_2 close to 1 independent of the problem, and a decaying or small constant step size, converges to stationary points on smooth nonconvex finite-sum objectives under standard noise assumptions, and explain the empirical advantage of Adam over SGD on transformer losses in a provable model.
rows.statement_caveat: Many partial results (problem-dependent hyperparameters, bounded gradients, affine noise) exist.
rows.source: S. J. Reddi, S. Kale and S. Kumar, On the Convergence of Adam and Beyond, arXiv:1904.09237 (2019); Y. Zhang, C. Chen, N. Shi, R. Sun and Z.-Q. Luo, Adam Can Converge Without Any Modification On Update Rules, arXiv:2208.09632 (2022)
rows.locator: to verify: Zhang et al., the discussion of problem-dependent beta_2.
rows.why_important: Adam trains nearly every large model; its convergence in the regime used is still not established.
rows.note: Fame: Reddi et al. was an ICLR 2018 best paper.

rows.title: Overconfidence of overparameterized classifiers
rows.domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
rows.statement: Bai, Mei, Wang and Xiong prove that logistic regression fitted by maximum likelihood in the proportional regime (n, d → ∞, n/d fixed) is overconfident: its predicted probabilities exceed the true conditional probabilities, even without overparameterization. Prove a comparable theorem for a two-layer network trained by gradient descent on cross-entropy in a solvable regime (random features, or mean-field with a single-index teacher): characterize the calibration error as a function of n/d, width and training time, and show whether early stopping yields calibration.
rows.statement_caveat: Empirical overconfidence of modern networks is well documented (Guo et al. 2017); theory is limited to linear and random-features models (to verify).
rows.source: Y. Bai, S. Mei, H. Wang and C. Xiong, Don't Just Blame Over-parametrization for Over-confidence: Theoretical Analysis of Calibration in Binary Classification, arXiv:2102.07856 (2021)
rows.locator: to verify: Bai et al., conclusion (networks as open).
rows.why_important: Calibrated probabilities are what make a classifier's confidence usable; it is a question about the limiting law of a trained predictor's outputs.
rows.where_it_stands: Open for networks as far as the writer knows.
